Source says: Central Bank of Djibouti (Djibouti). Government of Djibouti appoints or directs the board of the Central Bank of Djibouti (Djibouti). Under the statutes set by law no. 118/AN/11/6eme L of 22 January 2011, the Banque Centrale de Djibouti's board is made up of the Governor and six administrators appointed by decree, so every seat other than the Governor's is filled by the executive. The bank's own 2024 annual report states that composition, calls the board the bank's supreme organ and cites the 2011 law, which shows the arrangement still stands. This is a standing arrangement with no end date. The record rests on the bank's annual report, not on the text of the law, which could not be obtained. Source says: Central Bank of the Comoros (Comoros). Government of the Union of the Comoros appoints or directs the board of the Central Bank of the Comoros (Comoros). Under the statutes of the Banque Centrale des Comores, signed in Paris on 22 April 2008 and still in force, the bank's board has at most eight members, half of them designated by the French Government and half by the Government of the Union of the Comoros, so every seat is filled by one of the two governments. The Governor is named by the President of the Union of the Comoros, on a proposal from the Minister of Finance. This is a standing arrangement with no end date; the bank's board approved a new draft of the statutes on 28 June 2024, but that text still awaited promulgation by the Union's President at the end of 2024. Statuts de la Banque Centrale des Comores (Banque Centrale des Comores)

A Lithuanian parliamentary commission chaired by Valentinas Mazuronis found that the Bank of Lithuania acted too fast and with too little reasoning when it shut down the bank Snoras in November 2011. Mazuronis said the takeover of Snoras shares in the public interest and the start of bankruptcy proceedings were both hasty and not sufficiently reasoned.
